content: 1. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and eluxadoline can prolong the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. If co-administration is necessary, close monitoring is required. 2. Eluxadoline increases the levels of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting its metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. In severe cases, alternative drugs should be considered. 3. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of eluxadoline by reducing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg orally twice daily and monitor closely. 4. The combination of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Cobicistat, a CYP3A4 inhibitor, is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that have a high risk of serious or life-threatening events due to elevated plasma concentrations. 5. Encorafenib affects CYP3A4 metabolism, both inhibiting and inducing it at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. It increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels and effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Encorafenib, as an OATP1B3 inhibitor, may also increase the concentration and toxicity of OATP1B3 substrates. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used, reduce the encorafenib dose by half (e.g., from 450 mg/day to 225 mg/day). 6. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and encorafenib prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. 7. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the effects of enoxaparin by reducing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 8. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases entrectinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors must be used with entrectinib, resume the previous entrectinib dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives. 9. Enzalutamide decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 10. Both epinephrine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. 11. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases eplerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Erdafitinib increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours before or after P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 13. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases ergotamine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 14. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and eribulin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 15. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases erlotinib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 16. Escitalopram increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 17. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 18. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases estradiol levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 19. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases eszopiclone levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption and affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the eszopiclone starting dose to 1 mg/day and monitor closely. 20. Ethanol decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 21. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. Antibiotics may reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 22. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases etonogestrel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 23. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases etoposide levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Etravirine decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases etravirine levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 25. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases eucalyptus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases everolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration is contraindicated. 27. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases exemestane levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ezogabine increase QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, especially at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. ECG monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is prescribed with QT-prolonging agents. 29. Fedratinib increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 30. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases felodipine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 31. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases fentanyl levels (intranasal, transdermal, transmucosal) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. 32. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases fesoterodine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 33. Fexinidazole increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 34. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases fexofenadine levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 35. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases finasteride levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases finerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 37. Both fingolimod and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 38. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and flecainide prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 39. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases flibanserin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Severe hypotension or syncope can occur. 40. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Fluconazole increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 41. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases fludrocortisone levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 42. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and fluoxetine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Both fluphenazine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 44. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases fluvastatin toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 45. Both fluvoxamine and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 46. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases fondaparinux effects by reducing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 47. Both erythromycin ethylsuccinate and formoterol prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs.
